summary.learning_goal: Explore relationships among head systems, brain regions and individual anatomical structures.
summary.primary_visualization: 708 aligned anatomical objects, hierarchical scope and paginated exploded views.
summary.primary_interaction: Open a system, explode into labeled parts, and compare a cutaway with the assembled head.

strengths: Original versus illustrative positions are labeled, and display settings state that open clipping surfaces are not medical scans.
weaknesses: Factual anatomy is not independently audited; mesh hierarchy is editorial and functional explanations are sparse.

strengths: Brain scope narrows 708 objects to 247; the 24-part page exposes named structures without showing everything at once.
weaknesses: Guided tour emphasizes layers and labels rather than why structures function; explosion normalizes sizes and changes spatial relations.

strengths: Detailed brain topology, contextual labels and a skull cutaway expose depth relationships.
weaknesses: Open cut surfaces and normalized part sizes require careful interpretation; a dense label inventory still needs zoom.

strengths: Hierarchy selection, reversible explosion and cutaway all caused visible geometry changes; the assembled brain returns from the inventory.
weaknesses: Controls are numerous; material and section-plane choices were exposed but not individually tested.

strengths: Large centered anatomy and edge controls maintain a coherent stage across scope changes.
weaknesses: On the captured 390×844 state the open Visualization panel covers much of the model; labels are small.

principles_to_learn: Use a hierarchy to let the learner choose the level of detail.
Page large part inventories and retain a breadcrumb to the whole.
Explain what a cutaway does and does not represent.
Offer a reversible transition between contextual and isolated views.
things_not_to_copy: Do not imply exploded objects retain true spacing or scale.
Do not copy the control density to a novice lesson.
golden_recommendation: Use for hierarchical dissection, exploded view, cutaway. Use principles with the documented limitations.
